slides.title: Why was SCTP Created?
slides.body:
Three images requested. Image 2's packet is lost. Image 3 is stuck waiting even though it arrived fine
Problem 1 — Head-of-Line (HOL) Blocking:
TCP delivers data as one ordered stream. If one segment is lost, all segments behind it wait — even if they already arrived correctly
Two Problems TCP Could Not Solve

slides.title: Why was SCTP Created?
slides.body:
Two Problems TCP Could Not Solve
Problem 2 — Single Path Dependency:
TCP binds a connection to one IP address per side
If that path fails, the entire connection drops and must restart from scratch
Critical problem for telecom signaling where availability cannot be interrupted

slides.title: SCTP — Stream Control Transmission Protocol
slides.body:
A Smarter Transport Protocol
SCTP is a connection-oriented, reliable Transport Layer protocol — like TCP, but with two additional capabilities

slides.title: SCTP — Stream Control Transmission Protocol
slides.body:
A Smarter Transport Protocol
One association carries multiple independent streams
A loss in Stream 1 does NOT block Stream 2 or Stream 3
Each stream has its own Stream Sequence Number (SSN)
Multi-Streaming:
Feature 1

slides.title: SCTP — Stream Control Transmission Protocol
slides.body:
A Smarter Transport Protocol
Both endpoints register multiple IP addresses at association setup
One is the Primary Path; others are Standby Paths
SCTP sends Heartbeat chunks to monitor standbys
If primary fails → automatically switches to standby. No reconnection is needed
Multi-Homing:
Feature 2

slides.title: SCTP
slides.body:
4-Way Handshake:
Why Cookie?
Server allocates no resources until the cookie is echoed back 
Fake INIT messages cannot exhaust server memory
This protects against a DoS (Denial of Service) attack — where an attacker sends thousands of fake connection requests to crash the server by exhausting its memory 
Since SCTP's server stores nothing until the cookie is echoed back, fake requests cause no harm

A video call needs smooth, real-time delivery — delay kills it
A software update runs in the background — a few extra seconds do not matter
Without QoS, the network treats both identically. The video call suffers

slides.title: Per-Class Treatment
slides.body:
3. Differentiated Services (DiffServ)
No per-flow tracking. Traffic sorted into classes at the network edge
Edge router marks each packet with a DSCP value (6-bit field in IP header)
Core routers only read the DSCP label and forward — no flow memory needed. Highly scalable

slides.title: QoS in Switched Networks (Local Network)
slides.body:
How Switches Prioritise Traffic?
QoS also works inside a local network — within your college, office, or data centre — using Ethernet switches

slides.title: QoS in Switched Networks (Local Network)
slides.body:
How Switches Prioritise Traffic
How Does a Switch Know Which Traffic is Priority?
Every Ethernet frame can carry a VLAN tag (802.1Q)
Inside this tag, there is a 3-bit field called PCP (Priority Code Point)
3 bits = 8 priority levels (0 to 7), where 7 is highest and 0 is lowest
Ethernet uses a standard called IEEE 802.1p to mark priority inside a local network

slides.title: How Switches Prioritise Traffic
slides.body:

slides.title: QoS in Switched Networks (Local Network)
slides.body:
How Switches Prioritise Traffic
How It Works:
When a VoIP packet enters the switch, it is tagged with PCP = 6
When a file download enters the switch, it is tagged with PCP = 0
The switch reads this PCP value and serves higher priority frames first from its queue
Result - even on a busy office network, voice calls stay clear
